tier_reason: First-party ledger (benchmarks/PERF-LEDGER.md) whose public harness benchmarks/matrix/bench_matrix.cpp races an in-process libyaml (pinned 90a56d4). Hardware is given only as 'Apple silicon' and no compiler or version is stated. No peer-reviewed or independent third-party suite exists, so the record's tier B does not hold.

corrections.claimed_speedup: PERF-LEDGER 'Baseline 2026-09-01 (Apple silicon, Release+LTO, --quick)' table, libyaml event parse = 1.0x: DOM 2.2-3.6x, pull 2.7-4.0x, recorder 2.8-4.1x (e.g. scalar-heavy DOM 3.6x, wide-mapping DOM 3.5x, realworld-suite DOM 2.9x). The 'emit' column (4.8-6.9x) divides yeptris_serialize output MB/s by libyaml's PARSE MB/s. libyaml's emitter is never timed, so the emit column is not an emit-vs-emit win. This is the earliest table in the ledger. Later ledger entries give DOM 1.85-3.57x, and the README headline is scalar-heavy up to 3.36x, block ~2.3x, wide ~2.4x, anchor-heavy ~1.8x.
corrections.workload: bench_matrix --quick uses seeded synthetic corpora (40k entries: block-heavy, flow-json, scalar-heavy, anchor-heavy, deep-nesting, wide-mapping) plus realworld-suite (libyaml snapshot files that both parsers accept), timed as min-of-3. yeptris DOM parse, pull, recorder, and serialize (emit from a pre-parsed DOM) are each divided by the same run's libyaml yaml_parser_parse event loop. libyaml builds no document, and its emitter is not measured.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: yeptris: CMake Release with LTO (IPO) on by default; compiler and version not stated. libyaml reference: a separate static libyaml.a linked into the harness. CI builds it CMake Release without LTO; the build type of the dev-box libyaml behind the quoted table is not stated.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 0 GitHub stars. The yeptris RubyGems gem (Ruby binding that vendors libyeptris) shows 136,902 total downloads per the rubygems.org API on 2026-09-25.
corrections.caveats: All ratios are self-measured, first-party numbers. Hardware is given only as 'Apple silicon', and no compiler version is stated. The quoted table is the 2026-09-01 min-of-3 --quick snapshot of early code. Later ledger entries report lower DOM ratios (1.85-3.57x), and the README headline is 1.8-3.36x. The emit column divides yeptris serializer output throughput (bytes of output) by libyaml parse throughput, so it says nothing about libyaml's emitter. The timing is asymmetric: the libyaml timing includes parser teardown, while the yeptris DOM, pull, and recorder timings exclude their free calls. yeptris also gets LTO and libyaml does not. The ledger records a 1.35x floor on the first shared-runner CI run and repeated dev-box load and thermal noise. The ledger text calls flow-json DOM 2.5x the weakest cell, but anchor-heavy DOM 2.2x in the same table is lower. Current CI artifacts (run 36118925445, v0.6.22) show DOM 1.61-7.72x (ubuntu) and 2.09-6.99x (macOS), and pull 1.36-2.80x and 1.64-3.46x, against the libyaml parse. These CI numbers are not on the benchmark page.

notes: The claimed numbers match the ledger's 2026-09-01 baseline table verbatim, but tier B was wrong: every number is first-party, so the tier is C. Reading the harness code shows that the 'emit vs libyaml' ratios compare serializing against libyaml parsing, and the quoted table is the earliest, highest snapshot. GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION, but LICENSE.md ('Ribose's BSD 2-Clause License', Ribose Inc) is the standard BSD-2-Clause text. The last commit is 2026-09-25 (v0.6.22); the repo is not a fork and not archived.
